notes:
User is building consistent weekend and bedtime routines. They now plan to wake around 7:30 a.m. on Saturdays, have coffee, and start a 30-minute jog around 8:15–8:30 a.m. They live in a downtown area and want a relatively flat route with shade, preferably a park, riverside path, tree-lined street, covered bike trail, or quieter side street. They plan to use route-finding tools and check for water fountains/drinking stations. They prefer leaving earbuds behind to remain aware of traffic, cyclists, and other hazards. After jogging, they want guidance on cooling down; suggestions include gradually slowing to a walk for 5–10 minutes, gentle stretching, light mobility, hydration, and refueling.

On Sundays, they plan to wake around 8:30, do 30 minutes of gentle yoga/stretching to loosen up after a week of desk sitting, then have a quick breakfast and meal prep for the week. They prefer starting small and gradually increasing routines as they become comfortable.

User has a desk job and wants accessible, low-intensity morning exercise. They are interested in entrepreneurship and startup building, especially rapid experimentation, customer feedback, and iteration. They chose *The Lean Startup* by Eric Ries as a starting book and want to apply Build-Measure-Learn and related concepts—MVPs, validation, pivoting, metrics, innovation accounting, and entrepreneurial management—to their own projects.

User wants to read for 30 minutes before bed nightly, beginning with *The Lean Startup*. Helpful habits include a quiet, distraction-free space, a small session goal, 25 minutes reading plus a 5-minute break, brief notes, summarizing in their own words, visualizing concepts, reviewing takeaways, and connecting material to personal projects. To keep it low-friction, turn off notifications, use a physical book or offline e-reader, stay hydrated, and protect sleep.
